title: Text embedding models
subtitle: I ran a bake-off across embedding families for retrieval and replaced an incumbent chosen by habit with one chosen by measurement.

lede: Capabilities model needed a retrieval baseline strong enough that beating it would mean something. The incumbent embedding model had been picked only because the rest of the estate used it. I had a bake-off run on the frozen evaluation. The candidates went through the same harness on ONNX Runtime, and disqualifiers for latency and context length stopped an accurate but undeployable model from winning. The winner went into a fusion baseline with BM25. GPU scoring runs with TF32 pinned off, after a known-answer control showed that the precision setting changed rankings. The models are third-party open models; the bake-off, the serving architecture and the retrieval design are mine. See The baseline that tied us.
evidence: Embedding model selection: a bake-off of 5 embedding models through one harness on the frozen evaluation, with latency and context-length disqualifiers.
Retrieval baselines: a BM25 and dense fusion baseline with every weight chosen by sweep, built as strong as it honestly could be even where it tied my own model.
Embedding serving architecture: a multilingual 568M-parameter embedder moved from an in-process Python bridge to its own server, producing 1,024-dimension vectors.
author: Corey James
